caption:
The AI built the price sort for a product list. The button works, nothing errors, and the list comes back in the same order.

Look at the card. sort() wants a number from the compare function: negative means a goes first, positive means b goes first, 0 means keep them as they are. a.price > b.price returns true or false, which count as 1 or 0. It never returns a negative number, so the engine is never told to move anything. In Chrome and Node the list stays as it was. Other engines may give a different, still wrong, order.

Fix: return a.price - b.price for low to high, b.price - a.price for high to low.

Source: MDN, Array.prototype.sort() (compareFn).
